findings.reason: “Kuscheln” means to cuddle or snuggle, not to pat.
“Field” is a noun; “ländlich” means rural or relating to the countryside.
A Landstraße is generally a country road, not a highway.
“Längs” is a preposition/adverb meaning along, not long.
“Leertaste” means the space bar; “long” is an erroneous addition.
“Lehnen” means to lean, often against something, not to push.
“Leine” is a leash or lead; “accompany” is an unrelated verb.

findings.currentEn: A small truck for the removal of goods
findings.reason: A Lieferwagen is a vehicle for delivering goods, not removing them.
The German noun refers to a person, not the adjective alone.
Locke means a curl of hair; “sprung” is unrelated.
A German Loge is a theatre box, not generally a lodge.
With plural Male, Mal normally means a time or occasion.
Mangeln is a verb meaning “to lack”; “missing” is not the base verb.
Maßnahme means a measure or action taken, not an event.

findings.recommendedEn: For my sake; if you like
findings.reason: Meinetwegen means “for my sake” or “if you like,” not “after me.”
“Psychoterror” is not the usual English equivalent of German “Mobbing.”

findings.currentEn: Salary of a clerk or servant
findings.reason: The English does not convey “monthly” and adds an unsupported job meaning.
“Mondschein” means light from the moon, not a house.
“Piggies” is not the English name of the disease.

findings.recommendedEn: Catch up on what was missed
findings.reason: The current phrase is ungrammatical and does not express the verb naturally.
“Nachteil” means disadvantage or drawback, not generally “loss.”
The English is an incomplete compound fragment and does not translate the adjective.
“Scoundrel” is unrelated; Nacken means the back of the neck or nape.
“Next thing” does not mean a secondary or unimportant matter.
“Nebula” is a noun for a cloud in space; neblig is the adjective “foggy.”
“Squeal” is unrelated; necken means to tease or make fun of.
The current phrase is unnatural and does not convey the usual meaning of Notfall.
“Vain” usually means conceited or futile; nutzlos means “useless.”
“Opera” is the performance or art form; Opernhaus means the building or venue.
The German singular refers to a one-piece work garment; the current plural is mismatched.
Panne means a breakdown or mishap, not a quibble.
Palast means palace, whereas castle is Burg or Schloss.
Parterre refers to the ground level of a building.
The German word Paste means paste; mail is the meaning of German Post.
Peinlich usually describes something embarrassing or awkward.
The English field contains the Latvian word “pa” instead of the English preposition.
Personalabteilung means the department responsible for personnel or human resources.
Pfarrer means a pastor or parish priest, not a teacher.
Pflügen means to plow; “art” is unrelated.
Pier means pier; mole is a different English word.
“Plump” means slightly fat or chubby, not someone who eats too much.
“Poltern” means to make loud banging noises, not to grind.

findings.currentEn: Subscription box at the post office
findings.reason: “Postfach” means a rented mailbox or post office box.
“Prozentsatz” means a percentage or percentage rate, not an interest rate.
“Prüfzeit” refers to a testing or examination period, not probation.
“Wheel rail” is not the meaning of Radspur; it refers to a track made by a wheel.
Ragen means to protrude or project, not to lean.
Ratlos means unable to decide or unsure what to do, not distracted.
Rauben generally means to rob or steal; “to kidnap” is a different verb.
Reh means roe deer; a doe is any adult female deer and is less specific.
